newsitem.title: CROATIA: CROATIAN STOCKS FIRMER, MILD GROWTH SEEN LASTING.
newsitem.headline: CROATIAN STOCKS FIRMER, MILD GROWTH SEEN LASTING.

text.p: Croatian stocks scored new gains on Tuesday in moderate summer trade, featuring food processor Podravka, and traders expected mild growth to last for a while.

"It is a shorter week and trade has contracted because of holidays. But having said that, volumes are quite decent, supporting the growth trend of most stocks," said one trader who asked not to be named.
He cited Podravka, hoteliers Laguna and Riviera among the likely gainers in the next two days ahead of Friday's market closure due to a bank holiday.
Eleven of 18 active issues rose, five -- including blue chips Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka -- fell, two closed flat and one traded for the first time.
Volume shrank slightly to 14,004 units, but turnover rose to 16 from 6.4 million kuna last Friday, when heavyweight Zagrebacka was poorly traded.
Both blue chips had led a strong market rally over the past three weeks with a series of almost daily historic highs. But their luck seems to have turned.
Zagrebacka's ordinary stock lost 4.90 kuna to end at 2,500.10 on volume of 2,528 units. Trade in its 1/10 Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) on Seaq stalled at $39.125.
Pliva, closing 3.25 percent lower at 595 kuna with only 58 shares sold, took some beating after its 1/5 GDRs also dipped slightly from the open to around $18.44 in London.
"It won't be for long, but Pliva may stagnate for a while," the trader, who serves a number of foreign clients, said.
"Zagrebacka Banka is likely to fluctuate around 2,500 kuna and that will last until a new significant development," he said referring to the release of first half earnings, due in September.
The day's gainers were led by recently overhauled Rijecka Banka, rising 35 kuna or 35 percent to 135 kuna from late in July when it last traded on the bourse. It sold 500 shares.
But trader Velimir Zelimorski of brokerage Fima pointed out the most active Podravka with 3,649 shares, for its steady recovery from a longish depression.

It followed rumours about poor 1996 results which were not countered by the company at all. Instead, Podravka hinted it was interested in purchasing some of its stock, when it traded at around 250 kuna early in July.
Its shares rose three kuna on Wednesday to 290 kuna -- the price it was expected to maintain for about two weeks, when a stronger new growth cycle could begin.
Hotelier Riviera, losing eight kuna or 4.37 percent to 175 kuna with 806 shares traded, was the biggest decliner. But its losses were seen as temporary.
